original_query: select  i_item_id,         s_state, grouping(s_state) g_state,         avg(ss_quantity) agg1,         avg(ss_list_price) agg2,         avg(ss_coupon_amt) agg3,         avg(ss_sales_price) agg4 from store_sales, customer_demographics, date_dim, store, item where ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk and       ss_item_sk = i_item_sk and       ss_store_sk = s_store_sk and       ss_cdemo_sk = cd_demo_sk and       cd_gender = 'F' and       cd_marital_status = 'W' and       cd_education_status = 'College' and       d_year = 1999 and       s_state = 'WI' and      i_category  = 'Music'  group by rollup (i_item_id, s_state)  order by i_item_id          ,s_state  limit 100;
rewritten_query:
select i_item_id,
       s_state,
       grouping(s_state) g_state,
       avg(ss_quantity) agg1,
       avg(ss_list_price) agg2,
       avg(ss_coupon_amt) agg3,
       avg(ss_sales_price) agg4
from store_sales ss
join customer_demographics cd on ss.ss_cdemo_sk = cd.cd_demo_sk
join date_dim d on ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
join store s on ss.ss_store_sk = s.s_store_sk
join item i on ss.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
where cd_gender = 'F'
  and cd_marital_status = 'W'
  and cd_education_status = 'College'
  and d_year = 1999
  and s_state = 'WI'
  and i_category = 'Music'
group by rollup (i_item_id, s_state)
order by i_item_id,
         s_state
limit 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Convert implicit comma joins into explicit INNER JOINs with join predicates attached, making the join graph clear and enabling the optimizer to push dimension filters (s_state='WI', d_year=1999, i_category='Music') into selective dimension scans before the fact-table join.

All dimension attribute filters (cd_gender='F', cd_marital_status='W', cd_education_status='College', d_year=1999, s_state='WI', i_category='Music') are retained in WHERE; they are highly selective and can be evaluated on small dimension tables (store has only 102 rows, date_dim year filter yields ~365 rows) before probing the large fact table.

Keep GROUP BY ROLLUP (i_item_id, s_state) unchanged: since s_state is constrained to 'WI', detail and subtotal rows are correctly produced and ROLLUP computes all grouping sets in a single aggregation pass. Ordering and LIMIT semantics are preserved.

Recommended supporting composite index: store_sales (ss_store_sk, ss_sold_date_sk, ss_item_sk, ss_cdemo_sk) INCLUDE (ss_quantity, ss_list_price, ss_coupon_amt, ss_sales_price). s_state='WI' is the most selective filter (~few of 102 stores), so leading with ss_store_sk lets the plan start from the filtered store dimension instead of scanning all 1999 store_sales rows.
